notes: Phase 3 gate: V2 text mode, the baseline of the element channel alone. KS statistic 0.033679 at significance 0.621991 over 500 trials, against the P2b sketch reference v2-dev-wit-ab193017 at 0.0405 / 0.385035. Mean p 0.5063, variance 0.0901. Anderson-Darling p 0.589 and Cramer-von Mises p 0.361 show no shape departure. The discretization lattice contributes only 0.00094 of the statistic (2.8%) and inflates rather than deflates the null, so the statistic measures the distribution. The conditional row is clean - 0.4948 at decoy_count 219 against 0.5051 at 224, every group inside 0.8 standard errors of 0.5 - where the sketch reference recorded 0.2477 against 0.5163. FINDING, recorded as standing: the clean conditional row is a coincidence of which images sit in the near-duplicate group, not the P2b defect disappearing. The per-image commonness leak is present in this channel too. Sorting the 500 trials by their target's element commonness gives quintile mean p 0.4252 / 0.4658 / 0.5259 / 0.5097 / 0.6052, trial-level Spearman +0.2053 (t 4.68, n 500, p 3.7e-06); the sketch reference measures +0.4722 against its outline table, so the element channel carries about 43% of the outline channel's leak. The mechanism is structural, not a bug: the architecture section 13.1 correction 2*raw - commonness removes about half of a baseline offset by construction, and the commonness table is built from source A alone (1,000 dataset captions) where architecture section 13.2 names source B the more important one. Source B arrives with the Phase 4 synthetic submission generator; reducing this per-image slope should be one of its acceptance criteria. The marginal distribution is uniform, so this does not fail V2. A raised caveat on the trial-score variance sitting 1.8 standard errors high was withdrawn under verification: exact two-sided p 0.068, one of about eight statistics computed on this run, and indistinguishable from the passed sketch reference over the identical 500 pairs.
